newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Horizon/CMS says Q2 estimates reasonable.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Horizon/CMS says Q2 estimates reasonable.

text.p: Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp Chief Financial Officer Ernest Schofield said Tuesday he was comfortable with estimates that second-quarter earnings per share would fall between $0.25 and $0.28.
"I think that's a reasonable range," Schofield said in a telephone interview with Reuters. The First Call consensus of analysts' estimates put the range at $0.25 to $0.28.

Schofield said the company's performance in the second quarter ending November 30 was being hurt by disappointing occupancy rates in its skilled nursing facilities and "volume pressures" in its contract therapy operations.
"There's been some operating pressure in a number of areas of the business," Schofield said.
He said he expected a modest increase in revenue in the second quarter after a 2.8 percent gain in the first quarter.
Horizon/CMS share price has declined amid concern over shareholder lawsuits and investigations into the company by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock was trading on Tuesday afternoon at 12-1/4, down from its year-high of 28.
"Until there is some resolution and clarity on those issues, I don't expect that the stock is going to dramatically jump," Schofield said.
He said he hoped the legal ramifications would become clearer by May 31, 1997, the end of Horizon/CMS's fiscal year.
He declined further comment on the legal cases and investigations.
